scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Naleyo is rooted among the Karamajong people, an agro-pastoral ethnic group living in North Eastern Uganda who speak the Nilotic language NgaKarimojong.
The dance functions as an annual post-harvest custom, emerging from seasonal rhythms to provide a structured gathering for celebration and social bonding.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Naleyo is held annually after the harvest season as a wooing and courtship celebration.
It provides a recognized cultural venue for young men and women to find love and select suitors, while serving as a broader expression of Karamajong cultural heritage.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in two parallel lines with women in one line and men arranged in the opposite line facing one another.
Dancers face each other across the divide and execute energetic, high vertical jumps.
In this setting, women actively choose their male dancing partners as the two lines interact.
Watch for High courtship leap.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Two opposing linear ranks positioned facing each other in an open communal space.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Accompaniment is provided by traditional instruments, specifically the adungu (arched harp), the ngoma (drum), and the ekitirikiti (shakers or percussive instruments).
These instruments supply the melodic and rhythmic backdrop that drives the dancers' repeated vertical leaps.
Listen for the adungu, ngoma, ekitirikiti.
The sonic signature is driven by the acoustic resonance of the adungu harp intertwined with the rhythmic, grounded beat of the ngoma drum and the sharp, rustling percussion of the ekitirikiti.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Form two opposing, parallel lines with men in one line and women in the other, directly facing across the floor.
Step 2: Engage the core and bend both knees to prepare an explosive vertical rebound.
Footwork from the sources: Two-footed takeoff and landing executing continuous high vertical jumps facing an opposing line.
Drill: Stand facing an opposite partner at a distance of three meters with shoulders relaxed.
on_screen: Instructor front view, then back view (student's perspective); repetitions per step: about 4
Counts on screen

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Jump straight up off both feet, driving vertically into the air while keeping the torso upright and maintaining eye contact with the opposite line.
Step 4: Land softly on the balls of both feet with knees flexed, keeping the rhythm steady.
Drill: Practice rhythmic knee bounces and ankle pre-loading without leaving the floor.
on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Maintain direct forward gaze to simulate courtship engagement across the line.
on_screen: Split screen: front view / back view
Tempo label changes: slow → half → full

scenes.title: Common mistakes and what to avoid
narration: Avoid stiff-legged landings or collapsing forward at the waist; ensure joint absorption on each descent.
on_screen: Side-by-side: wrong / right
